scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: SH-CS requested building an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (CL-01, initial_request).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume rose from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026), roughly doubling (E-03).
Ticket response times remain within the 3.0-day SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d), so response speed is not breaching standard (E-01).
~41% (1240 of 3025) of disputed bills are tied to ESTIMATED reads rather than ACTUAL reads (E-02).
Manual-read route completion for 9200 accounts is 0.88 against a 0.95 target in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-05).
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Since August 2026 Lakeside's billing dispute ticket volume has roughly doubled (E-03), not because ticket response is slow — response times remain within the 3.0-day SLA (E-01), contradicting the initial framing (CL-01) — but because manual field meter-read routes for 9200 accounts are completing at 0.88 against a 0.95 target (E-05), leaving reads missing for billing's estimate-substitution step (process P-M2C), and a substantial share of disputed bills (1240 of 3025, ~41%) are tied to these ESTIMATED reads rather than ACTUAL reads (E-02): customers receiving estimate-substituted bills are disproportionately disputing them, driving the surge.

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-02 revised by E-12: The observation still stands: 1240 disputed bills are tied to ESTIMATED reads vs 1785 ACTUAL (E-02), and this 1240 exactly matches E-12's AMI-channel breakdown. It no longer means this estimate-substituted population traces to missing manual field reads (PR-ROOT) — E-12 shows it is AMI-channel, 95.5% caused by billing-import REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, not field-route no-read.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

steps: read collection (AMI interval read or field manual read)
estimate substitution when no accepted read

F-02.statement: Disputed bills by read type (E-02): 1240 on ESTIMATED reads, 1785 on ACTUAL reads.

F-04.statement: billing-db tariff_change_log returned 0 records, indicating no tariff changes were logged in the queried period.

F-05.statement: Field route completion for manual-read accounts (9200) was 0.88 against a 0.95 target for period 2026-08..09.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 permits the utility to request route priority changes, executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-07.statement: route-log.lagging_routes returned 14 records with distinct per-route completion values; sample shows route R-00 at 0.70 completion.

F-08.statement: billing-db accounts_estimated_last_cycle (E-10) returned 320 records across 40 distinct routes for the current cycle (sample account AC-20000, route R-00), with fields limited to account_id and route and no dispute status.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-SPEED.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a ticket-handling/response-capacity problem; an AI agent that auto-answers tickets (and performs ad hoc bill fixes) would resolve it.

H-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-SURGE.statement: A rise in bills issued via estimate substitution (used when no accepted read is available) since August is producing systematically incorrect bills and driving disputes.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August is causing valid reads to be rejected or mis-imported, producing incorrect bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: Manual field meter reads from the contracted vendor are failing or being delayed since August, causing missing/estimated reads and incorrect bills.

H-AMI-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: AMI/MDMS nightly export of interval reads is failing or delivering invalid data since August (vendor-side), feeding bad or missing reads into billing.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECTION.statement: Billing import validation rejects AMI reads flagged as high consumption (billing_import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) even when received before cutoff and exported, forcing estimate substitution and directly accounting for ~1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: CRM data (2440 tickets) shows median response time of 1.6 days and p90 of 2.8 days, both under the 3.0-day SLA, indicating ticket response speed is not breaching the service standard; this undercuts the premise that slow/inadequate response handling is the surge's cause.

Of disputed bills broken out by read type (E-02), 1240 are tied to ESTIMATED reads and 1785 to ACTUAL reads, so a substantial minority (~41%) of disputes are associated with estimate-substituted bills rather than actual meter reads. This is consistent with estimate substitution being a meaningful driver of disputes, but it does not by itself show a change since August or identify why those reads were estimated instead of actual.

The observation still stands: 1240 disputed bills are tied to ESTIMATED reads vs 1785 ACTUAL (E-02), and this 1240 exactly matches E-12's AMI-channel breakdown. It no longer means this estimate-substituted population traces to missing manual field reads (PR-ROOT) — E-12 shows it is AMI-channel, 95.5% caused by billing-import REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, not field-route no-read.

crm-tickets.dispute_volume_monthly shows disputes went from 610/590 in Jun/Jul 2026 to 1180/1260 in Aug/Sep 2026, confirming the ticket volume roughly doubled starting in August as the initial request claimed; this validates the surge's existence and timing but is silent on its cause.

The billing-db tariff_change_log query returned zero records, meaning no tariff changes were logged around the dispute surge window; this rules out a tariff change as a contributor to the incorrect/disputed bills.

Field route-log data shows manual-read route completion of 0.88 against a 0.95 target for 9200 manually-read accounts over 2026-08..09, i.e. a 7-point shortfall. This is consistent with field manual reads being incomplete/delayed, which would feed missing reads into billing, but the single-period snapshot alone does not establish that this is a change from a pre-August baseline.

The observation still stands: manual-read route completion was 0.88 against a 0.95 target for 9200 accounts over 2026-08..09 (E-05) — the field route shortfall itself is unrevised. It no longer means this shortfall feeds the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills counted in E-02 — E-12 shows that disputed-estimated population is AMI-channel and import-rejection driven, not missing-manual-read driven, so the assumed route-to-billing dataset link (A-ROUTE-BILLING-DATASET-LINK) is undermined for this population.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states no tariff change occurred this year, which as a stakeholder claim corroborates the already-recorded authoritative finding (E-04) that the tariff_change_log has zero entries; it adds no new decision-relevant information beyond confirming agreement.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (Field Operations Manager, who has a stated incentive for contract headcount increase and a noted bias toward attributing problems to staffing) claims a 3-reader staffing shortfall since July causes late routes, which in turn produce estimated bills for affected customers; this is an unverified stakeholder claim, not a confirmed fact, and offers a candidate causal mechanism behind the route lateness already observed in E-05.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-08 is an authoritative document (service contract §4.2) establishing that route priority changes may be requested by the utility but must be executed only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager; it is a governance/authority document, not evidence about the dispute surge's cause.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: The route-log lagging_routes query (E-09) identifies 14 distinct routes each with its own completion value (sample: route R-00 at 0.70), showing the aggregate 0.88 Aug-Sep shortfall (E-05) is spread across multiple specific routes rather than a single outlier. It confirms route-level granularity of the field read completion gap but says nothing about why these routes lag (staffing vs. another cause) or about any pre-August baseline.

E-10.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db's accounts_estimated_last_cycle query (E-10) returned 320 accounts across 40 distinct routes that received estimate-substituted reads in the current cycle, but the record only contains account_id and route fields — no dispute status — so it does not by itself complete the intended correlation between estimate substitution and disputes (W-ESTIMATE-CORR).

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (ORG-AMI) claims MDMS export access for Lakeside is now provisioned (vendor ticket TX-4471), which if true removes the ACCESS_PENDING blocker on querying mdms-export for AMI read events; it is a stakeholder claim about access status only, not evidence about AMI delivery health or the dispute surge's cause.

U-AMI-DELIVERY-CONTRIBUTION.question: Does AMI/MDMS nightly export delivery to billing also contribute missing/invalid reads (H-AMI-DELIVERY-FAILURE), given mdms-export is DEGRADED and vendor access is pending?
U-AMI-DELIVERY-CONTRIBUTION.decision_impact: If AMI delivery is also failing, scope must add AMI-side investigation/remediation; if not, scope stays limited to the field-read side.
U-AMI-DELIVERY-CONTRIBUTION.resolution_path: Obtain vendor-provisioned MDMS export access (per DA-MDMS acquisition note) and query mdms-export read events for disputed/estimated accounts.
U-AMI-DELIVERY-CONTRIBUTION.safe_placeholder: Treat field-read incompleteness as the primary confirmed driver; do not assume AMI delivery is or isn't also failing until queried.
U-AMI-DELIVERY-CONTRIBUTION.resolution: E-12 shows AMI/MDMS export delivery is largely intact (only 56/1240 records are true NO_READ_RECEIVED); the dominant contributor (1184/1240) is billing import REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION on reads already received and exported, so AMI delivery failure explains only a small part of missing/invalid reads.

U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CONTRIBU.safe_placeholder: Proceed without assuming a rule change occurred; keep as an untested alternate contributor.

U-ROUTE-SHORTFALL-ROOT-CAUSE.question: Is the manual-read route completion shortfall caused by the reader staffing shortage SH-FIELD claims, or by another operational cause?

U-ROUTE-SHORTFALL-ROOT-CAUSE.resolution_path: Compare route completion and staffing-level trends before/after July 2026 using route-log data.
U-ROUTE-SHORTFALL-ROOT-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Do not assume staffing shortage is the cause; keep any route-update action open pending data and subject to K-DISPATCH human confirmation.

U-PRE-AUGUST-ROUTE-BASELINE.question: What was manual-read route completion before August 2026 — is 0.88 a decline or a pre-existing level?
U-PRE-AUGUST-ROUTE-BASELINE.decision_impact: Affects whether route completion is a genuine 'since August' causal factor or a longer-standing condition unrelated to the surge's timing.
U-PRE-AUGUST-ROUTE-BASELINE.resolution_path: Pull route-log completion history for months prior to August 2026.
U-PRE-AUGUST-ROUTE-BASELINE.safe_placeholder: Treat the Aug-Sep 0.88 figure as the current state without asserting it is a change from baseline.

A-ROUTE-BILLING-DATASET-LINK.statement: The field route completion shortfall (E-05) is assumed to be the operational source of the estimate-substituted bills counted in E-02, since the route and billing datasets have not been joined at the account level.

A-SHORTFALL-IS-CHANGE-SINCE-AU.statement: The 0.88 Aug-Sep completion rate (E-05) is assumed to represent a decline from a pre-August baseline, since E-05 is only a single-period snapshot.

hypotheses.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a ticket-handling/response-capacity problem; an AI agent that auto-answers tickets (and performs ad hoc bill fixes) would resolve it.
hypotheses.rationale: SH-CS requested exactly this solution and carries the noted potential_bias of framing issues as response-speed problems; this conflates handling tickets with fixing the underlying cause of wrong bills, and K-BILLWRITE forbids automated bill writes outright.

hypotheses.statement: A rise in bills issued via estimate substitution (used when no accepted read is available) since August is producing systematically incorrect bills and driving disputes.
hypotheses.rationale: The meter-to-cash process (P-M2C) explicitly includes an 'estimate substitution when no accepted read' step; whether this step's frequency rose in Aug-Sep is checkable against billing and read data.

hypotheses.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August is causing valid reads to be rejected or mis-imported, producing incorrect bills.
hypotheses.rationale: DA-RULES is the authoritative billing import validation rule change log and could show a configuration change timed near the August onset of the dispute surge; any fix would route through SH-BILL's manual-adjustment authority under K-BILLWRITE.

hypotheses.statement: Manual field meter reads from the contracted vendor are failing or being delayed since August, causing missing/estimated reads and incorrect bills.
hypotheses.rationale: H-FIELD-BILL is the manual-read handoff with UNKNOWN delivery_status and semantic_validity, and SH-FIELD's incentive is noted as pushing for contract headcount increase with a bias to attribute problems to staffing, so this hypothesis must be tested against actual completion data rather than assumed.

hypotheses.statement: AMI/MDMS nightly export of interval reads is failing or delivering invalid data since August (vendor-side), feeding bad or missing reads into billing.
hypotheses.rationale: H-MDMS-BILL is the nightly AMI export handoff with UNKNOWN delivery_status and semantic_validity, DA-MDMS access requires vendor provisioning, and ORG-AMI is an external dependency, making this a plausible and independently testable cause.
